hook: Crocker Galleria, whose barrel-vaulted arcade answers Milan's Galleria Vittorio Emanuele II.

building.name: Crocker Galleria
building.architect: Edward Charles Bassett of Skidmore, Owings & Merrill
building.completed_conflict: The assessor records 165 Sutter Street's year built as 1983; Wikipedia and SPUR's POPOS guide both give Crocker Galleria's opening year as 1982.

public_open_space.name: Crocker Galleria
public_open_space.location: Third floor of shopping center, down dark hallway.
public_open_space.landscaping: 8 large planter with trees, shrubbery around edge planters.
public_open_space.signage: No. Sign in interior atrium only says "roof garden"

permit_summary.note: DBI holds 180 permits for this parcel, most of them tenant improvements on individual floors. The timeline shows the 24 largest by stated cost, plus the earliest on file; the DBI query in the sources below returns all 180.

sections.heading: Two rooftops
sections.body: The open space is two sun terraces rather than one, and the further of them sits on the historic bank building at Montgomery and Post, reached by stairs or a lift.

historic_survey.note: Crocker Galleria by Skidmore, Owings & Merrill, its arched glass atrium part of the first major Postmodernist project downtown - and a shift signalled by one of the stalwart Modernist firms.
